summary.oneLiner: GRSE posted its best-ever year (FY26 revenue INR 7,002 cr, +38%; PAT INR 748 cr, +42%), executing fast enough to draw down its order book below INR 20,000 cr for the first time in 5 years. The investment case now hinges on order-book replenishment: a near-term NGC (Next Gen Corvette) contract worth ~INR 33,000 cr (L1, price negotiations complete, signing expected in Jun-2026 quarter) plus ~INR 1,50,000 cr of AoN-accorded RFPs on the anvil (excl. NGC). Margins have stepped up sharply (FY26 EBITDA ~11.6% vs FY25 ~8.3%), partly aided by provision write-backs; sustainability of double-digit margins through the NGC design-phase trough (FY27–FY28) is the key debate.

financial scorecard: Note: FY26 revenue cited as "best figures of 7,200" in one answer vs 7,002 stated in opening; opening 7,002 used as primary. Margin figures sourced from analyst Q&A and confirmed by mgmt. PYs derived from stated growth rates.
guidance: NGC contract signing expected in Q1 FY27 (Jun-2026 quarter); "no red flags."

NGC revenue recognition: nil in FY27; "mediocre" (design inputs) in H2 FY28; major chunk from FY29 (S-curve, ~65% of ship cost is equipment). Mgmt floated ~3-4-5% of NGC project cost recognised in FY28–29.
FY27 revenue accrual to be "very healthy, in line with last 3-4 years"; declined to confirm FY28 will avoid a dip — depends on order intake.
Margins: "will try to maintain similar margins" in FY27, FY28 and FY29 (i.e. ~11.5% region), but CMD would not commit to an exact number "only in the 1st Quarter."
Capacity: 28 platforms now → 32 by end of CY2026 via in-premises modernization.
order book & pipeline: Order book: INR 15,324 cr (9 projects, 39 platforms). ~95% shipbuilding (INR 14,730 cr); non-defence now 22.5% of total.
P-17A frigate: INR 5,868 cr remaining (1 ship left, ~74% progress, delivery in CY2026)
ASW SWC: INR 2,035 cr (4 of 8 delivered; 2 at ~80%, 2 at ~60%; project to finish FY27)
NGOPV (4 ships): INR 5,168 cr (1st launching 20-May; completion FY29)
→ Warship building total ~INR 11,361 cr

Non-defence: ORV INR 749 cr; Coastal Research Vessels (2) INR 260 cr; Acoustic Research Ship INR 456 cr; Hybrid Ferries (13) INR 207 cr; MPV (12, German export) INR 1,345 cr; Dredger (Bangladesh) INR 66 cr
On the anvil (AoN accorded, RFP/award pending) — total ~INR 1,50,000 cr excl. NGC:
NGC: ~INR 33,000 cr (L1, signing imminent) — not counted in the 1.5 lakh cr
7× P-17 Bravo frigates: ~INR 70,000 cr (split 4+3 between two yards, L1/L2); RFP expected within 3 months
12× Mine Countermeasure Vessels: AoN ~INR 32,000 cr (split 8+4); RFP H2 FY27
4× LPD: ~INR 35,000 cr (split 2+2); RFP H2 FY27
120 Fast Interceptor Craft: ~INR 3,500 cr (split 80+40); RFP within 3 months
31 Follow-On Water Jet FAC: ~INR 3,500 cr; RFP within 3 months
Live tenders: 2× MPV ~INR 1,500 cr (bid submitted); 5× NGOPV Coast Guard ~INR 2,000 cr; 22× Interceptor Boats Coast Guard ~INR 1,000 cr.
Commercial (Ministry of Shipping aggregated demand): 4 live tenders — 4 Platform Support Vessels (INR 1,200–1,500 cr), 4 MR tankers, 6 VLGCs, 6 Aframax vessels. Revitalization package ~INR 69,725 cr.
segment / subsidiary: Shipbuilding ~95% of order book; warships dominate value. Non-defence rose to 22.5% of order book (research vessels, ferries, export MPV, dredger).
Bridges vertical crossed INR 200 cr revenue for first time (110 portable steel bridges delivered, incl. 30 export).
Exports: >INR 270 cr revenue in FY26; active dialogue with European ship-owners shifting from China/Korea (capacity-full) to India on price + quality.
growth verticals: Commercial / export shipbuilding: entry via German 12-ship MPV; intends to follow with higher-margin, higher-value, complex hybrid/large vessels only. Strong European inbound interest.

Autonomous platforms: separate "new technology" business vertical, started ~3.5 yrs ago across subsurface/surface/aerial. Subsurface & surface versions developed; one product already supplied to a DRDO org. Part of Make-I/Make-II; eyeing XL-AUV Make project to materialise in 3-5 years.
Bridges: INR 200 cr+ milestone, export traction.
margins & cost: FY26 EBITDA margin ~11.6% (FY25 ~8.3%); analysts flagged Q4 FY25 & FY26 provision write-backs as a tailwind, pegging "sustainable" margins at ~9.5-10%. CMD repeatedly guided "similar margins" ahead without confirming the write-back-adjusted base.

All current projects on fixed-price contracts; vendor/subcontractor orders also fixed-price and placed early → minimal commodity escalation impact. Steel/industrial-gas delays "very marginal, insignificant," absorbed. New bids will explicitly factor commodity/time uncertainty.
~65% of a ship's cost is equipment; in NGC, ~55-60% of that equipment value is electronics (weapons/sensors) — large share to BEL.
capex: Expansion: 2 Brownfield yards (West Bengal) + 2 Greenfield yards (1 West Bengal, 1 Gujarat). In-premises modernization lifts capacity 28→32 platforms by end CY2026. Driven by govt shipbuilding revitalization package (~INR 69,725 cr) and Ministry of Shipping demand aggregation. No specific capex INR figure given on call.
capital allocation: No buyback/dividend specifics discussed on call. Capital directed at greenfield/brownfield capacity build to capture commercial + naval pipeline. Order-book gap to be "stemmed" by NGC1 plus 20-25% of balance anvil orders.
risks: Order-book drawdown below INR 20,000 cr; near-term FY27/FY28 revenue/margin trough during NGC design phase (operating de-leverage risk flagged by analyst).
NGC signing slipped from expected 31-Mar-2026 to Jun-2026 quarter — execution/timing risk on contract conversion.
Margin sustainability dependent on whether write-backs recur; CMD non-committal on exact figure.
Split-yard tenders (P-17B, MCMV, LPD, FAC) mean award is not guaranteed — competitive risk vs MDL/CSL/GSL.
Commodity escalation/time delays for new (not-yet-signed) contracts; VDS (variable depth sonar) is a buyer-furnished developmental item (no financial liability to GRSE, but a program dependency).
mgmt tone: Confident and detailed; CMD (Cmde Hari) gave granular order-by-order breakups and pipeline values. Notably candid that order book dropping below INR 20,000 cr is a positive (execution speed), and conservative on margin commitments ("will try to maintain," "can't say exact"). Reassured on his own continuity through FY27–FY28. Declined confidential weapon-fit questions.
non-obvious: Three warships delivered on a single day (claimed first in India's history) drove the large positive delta between 31-Mar provisional and final FY26 revenue — revenue recognition was held conservatively pending Navy liaison/handover.

Defence Standing Committee report showed near-2yr contract value for warships/survey vessels dropping from ~INR 42,000 cr to ~INR 18,900 cr; CMD argued this reflects annual fund-outflow timing, not intent — AoNs and RFPs continue.
NGC revenue is essentially a FY29 story, not FY28 — the "intermittent" gap is filled by OPV/commercial/research projects, not NGC.
BEL contract for NGC electronics expected 3-6 months after GRSE signs prime contract — read-through for BEL order inflow.
Conventional platforms defended as durable vs autonomous/drone narrative (armament, endurance >3 months at sea).
qoq change log: First GRSE concall note in this repository — no prior quarter baseline available for comparison. Establish FY26 figures (rev INR 7,002 cr, PAT INR 748 cr, EBITDA ~11.6%, order book INR 15,324 cr) as the baseline. Next quarter (Q1 FY27) to track: NGC contract signing confirmation, P-17B/FAC RFP releases, and any margin trajectory update.

themes.title: Naval shipbuilding & maritime
themes.need: A multi-decade naval order book and indigenous warship/submarine build, plus the naval-equipment supply chain (HVAC/chillers, mechanical seals, marine gearing) and maritime services, underpin the theme. GRSE carries a large RFP pipeline (~INR1.5 lakh cr referenced); SHREE REFRIGERATIONS 544458 supplies naval HVAC; SEALMATIC 543782 naval/submarine seals; ELECON defence-marine gearing; KMEW/SEAMECLTD/DREDGECORP maritime services.
themes.driver: Fresh MoD warship/submarine orders + naval-equipment indigenization inflow; maritime-infra/offshore contract wins.
